review_title: Tricyclic drugs for depression in children and adolescents
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing the efficacy of orally administered tricyclic drugs with placebo in depressed people aged 6 to 18 years.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset labels 1.0 and 0.5 count as INCLUDE; 0.0 counts as EXCLUDE

studies.predicted_reason: The intervention was administered intravenously (200 mg iv clomipramine). The selection criteria explicitly require orally administered tricyclic drugs. Route of administration disqualifies this study despite the RCT design and depressed adolescent population.

studies.study_title: A double‐blind, randomized, placebo‐controlled trial of fluoxetine in children and adolescents with depression
studies.predicted_reason: The pharmacological intervention is fluoxetine (an SSRI), not a tricyclic antidepressant. The selection criteria are limited to tricyclic drugs.

studies.study_title: Double‐blind placebo‐controlled study of nortriptyline in depressed adolescents using a "fixed plasma level" design
studies.predicted_reason: This is an RCT comparing nortriptyline (a tricyclic antidepressant) with placebo in depressed adolescents aged 12–17 years. Nortriptyline was administered orally (dose titrated to achieve target plasma levels). The study design, population, intervention, and comparison all meet the selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Childhood and adolescent depression: a review of the past 10 years. Part I
studies.predicted_reason: This is a qualitative review article summarising literature over a decade. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial and does not report original comparative efficacy data of a tricyclic versus placebo.

studies.study_title: Imipramine treatment of depressed children: a double‐blind pilot study
studies.predicted_reason: This double-blind pilot study compares oral imipramine with placebo in depressed children. Although the abstract does not state the exact age range, the term 'children' in this context typically refers to school-aged individuals likely falling within the 6–18-year range. The study includes both active and placebo arms with efficacy comparisons. Applying the conservative principle, this study should proceed to full-text review.

studies.study_title: Amitriptyline in children with major depressive disorder: a double‐blind crossover pilot study
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised, double-blind, crossover pilot study comparing oral amitriptyline with placebo in children aged 9–12 years with major depressive disorder. The study fully satisfies all selection criteria: RCT, oral tricyclic, placebo comparison, depressed population, and age 6–18 years.

studies.study_title: Newer generation antidepressants for depressive disorders in children and adolescents
studies.predicted_reason: This is a Cochrane review (or protocol) concerning newer generation antidepressants (SSRIs, etc.), not tricyclic drugs. It is not a primary RCT.

studies.study_title: Imipramine plus cognitive‐behavioural therapy in the treatment of school refusal
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised, double-blind trial comparing oral imipramine plus CBT with placebo plus CBT in school-refusing adolescents with comorbid major depressive disorder. Both arms receive the same psychosocial co-intervention, preserving the tricyclic versus placebo contrast. The population includes depressed individuals, depressive symptoms were measured, and the age group (adolescents) fits within 6–18 years.

studies.study_title: Imipramine in prepubertal major depressive disorders
studies.predicted_reason: Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of oral imipramine (up to 5 mg/kg/day) versus placebo in prepubertal children with major depressive disorder. 'Prepubertal' in this literature generally corresponds to ages 6–12, satisfying the age requirement. The study design and intervention meet all criteria.

studies.study_title: Efficacy of paroxetine treatment in the treatment of adolescent depression: a randomized, controlled trial
studies.predicted_reason: This three-arm RCT includes a direct comparison between oral imipramine (a tricyclic antidepressant) and placebo in adolescents with major depressive disorder. The presence of an additional paroxetine arm does not invalidate the tricyclic versus placebo comparison. The age group and diagnosis meet the selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Mechanism of action of antidepressant medications
studies.predicted_reason: Narrative review discussing pharmacological mechanisms. Not a primary RCT and provides no comparative efficacy data for a tricyclic versus placebo in the target population.

studies.study_title: SSRI safety in overdose
studies.predicted_reason: Observational review and safety analysis of SSRI overdose. Not an RCT of tricyclic drugs for depression in children or adolescents.

studies.study_title: Measuring inconsistency in meta‐analyses
studies.predicted_reason: Methodological paper on meta-analysis statistics. Not a clinical trial.

studies.study_title: Clinical, electrocardiographic, and laboratory findings in children with amitriptyline intoxication
studies.predicted_reason: Retrospective case series/review of amitriptyline poisoning. Not an RCT and does not evaluate antidepressant efficacy.

studies.study_title: The effect of concomitant disorders in childhood depression on predicting treatment response
studies.predicted_reason: This appears to be a secondary analysis focused on predictors of treatment response rather than a primary RCT report. The pharmacological agent is not identified as a tricyclic antidepressant, and the abstract does not confirm an RCT design comparing a tricyclic with placebo.

studies.study_title: Adolescent depression: controlled desipramine treatment and atypical features
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of oral desipramine (a tricyclic antidepressant) versus placebo in adolescents aged 13–18 years with major depressive disorder. Meets all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Psychopharmacology of child and adolescent major depression: present status and future directions
studies.predicted_reason: Narrative review and commentary article. Not a primary RCT.

studies.predicted_reason: The study population is defined by school refusal rather than by a diagnosis of depression. studies.study_title: Selected tricyclic antidepressant ingestions involving children 6 years old or less

studies.study_title: A randomized, controlled trial of amitriptyline in the acute treatment of adolescent major depression
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial of oral amitriptyline (5 mg/kg/day) versus placebo in adolescents aged 12–17 years with major depressive disorder. Fully meets all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: School phobia: a therapeutic trial with clomipramine and short‐term outcome
studies.predicted_reason: Double-blind trial of clomipramine in children with school phobia/neurotic disorder. The population was not selected for depression, and the primary disorder is school refusal. Does not meet the population criterion.

studies.study_title: Meta‐analysis of early phase II studies with paroxetine in hospitalised depressed patients
studies.predicted_reason: Meta-analysis of studies in hospitalised depressed adults aged 18–65 years. The age range is outside the 6–18-year target, and the comparison is paroxetine versus amitriptyline, not tricyclic versus placebo.

studies.study_title: Depression in children: relationship between plasma imipramine levels and response
studies.predicted_reason: Open-label or non-controlled study examining the relationship between plasma imipramine levels and clinical response. No placebo comparison group is described, so it is not an RCT comparing a tricyclic with placebo.

studies.study_title: Randomized, controlled trial of amitriptyline versus placebo for adolescents with "treatment‐resistant" major depression
studies.predicted_reason: Randomised, controlled trial comparing oral amitriptyline with placebo in adolescents with major depressive disorder. The study design, intervention, comparison, population, and age group all satisfy the selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Imipramine compliance in adolescents
studies.predicted_reason: This is a secondary report (compliance, side effects, and blinding assessment) derived from an RCT of imipramine versus placebo for school refusal. It does not present primary efficacy data, and the population is defined by school refusal rather than by depression.
